title: After the meeting with State govt on August 7, student leader Ravindra Paswan said: “It was the first round of meeting with the government and the government listened to our demands. However, we could not reach any conclusion regarding our key demands. Therefore, the protest will continue for the time being"
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
• August 08, 2026 11:09
    Student delegation arrives at State Guest House to meet government representatives

    Student delegation arrives at State Guest House to meet government representatives

  • August 08, 2026 11:08
    Student representatives leave for Circuit House for dialogue with government

    A designated delegation of the Student protestors in Jharkhand left for the Circuit House for dialogue with representatives of the Jharkhand Government regarding the demands of the aspirants.

    “The team has told us that we will go for a dialogue at the Circuit House at 10 a.m. Had the government agreed to our demands when the other students met them, then it wouldn’t have been necessary for us to go as well. It doesn’t matter how many of us go to meet them. All of us have the same demands, which should be fulfilled,” said Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto.- ANI

  • August 08, 2026 10:57
    All examinations conducted by the TDPL agency on behalf of the JPSC since 2022 should be cancelled: student delegation member

    Chandan Kumar, a student delegation member said, “...we want all examinations conducted by the TDPL agency on behalf of the JPSC since 2022 to be cancelled immediately. In addition, Abhay Tiwari, who was the marketing manager of the TDPL agency, appeared in several examinations, including the JSSC CGL and PGT examinations. Those examinations should also be cancelled.”- PTI

  • August 08, 2026 10:37
    Jharkhand CID summons three JPSC members on alleged govt. exam irregularities

    Jharkhand State Crime Investigation Department (CID) probing the case of alleged irregularities in the examination has now served notice to three serving members of Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC). The investigating agency has issued summons to three current JPSC members—Ajita Bhattacharya, Anima Hansda, and Jamal Ahmed and asked them to appear before the agency on August 10, 12, and 14, respectively. A crucial aspect of the investigation focuses on which grounds TSR Data Processing Private Limited (TDPL) —the agency that conducted the examination—was empanelled and selected, despite having been previously blacklisted.- Amit Bhelari

  • August 08, 2026 10:22
    We are going to stage a protest and gherao of the State Assembly on August 10: spokesperson, JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch

    Jivan Kumar Yadav, spokesperson, JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch, said, “Our plan today is that if the government invites us for talks again, our delegation will go and participate in the discussions. As you all may already know, we are going to stage a protest and gherao of the State Assembly on August 10. In this regard, students across Jharkhand will be called upon to participate. Shortly, our core committee will meet and finalise today’s programme, which will then be announced.” - PTI

  • August 08, 2026 10:06
    If our demands are not met, we will continue the hunger strike: student protestor Kush Mahto

    Student protestor Kush Mahto says, “We have decided on 10 people, possibly, five from each side. The dialogue would take place under the leadership of Devendra Mahto... If our demands are not met, we will continue the hunger strike. We are growing weaker by the day, losing energy, but our morale is not breaking... If Hemant Soren doesn’t fulfill our demands this time, students from all over Jharkhand will join our hunger strike.”- ANI.

  • August 08, 2026 10:00
    Years of delayed exams, bribery allegations provoke Jharkhand protests

    On July 23, students began gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi. They arrived carrying bedding, notebooks and plastic folders filled with admit cards from examinations that, in many cases, had defined nearly a decade of their lives. Their demand was straightforward: cancel all examinations tainted by allegations of corruption, order an independent investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and overhaul the state’s recruitment system.

    Read the full acticle,
  • August 08, 2026 09:54
    Meeting inconclusive between Jharkhand government and JPSS-JSCC Reform Manch

    A delegation of the Jharkhand Government comprising Ministers on Friday (August 7, 2026) held talks for the first time in State capital Ranchi with student protesters demanding an inquiry by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for alleged irregularities in competitive exams for government jobs. The two hour-long meeting, though, ended without any agreement with the students firm on continuing their protests.

    Read the full article,
  • August 08, 2026 09:51
    Stir enters 15th day in Jharkhand, govt. invites another faction of agitators for talks

    The seven members delegation of another group headed by Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) will meet the committee formed by the government on alleged irregularities in govt. exam on Saturday (August 8, 2026)- Amit Bhelari.

title: How does Supreme Court’s new handbook rethink gender sensitivity? | Explained
author: Aaratrika Bhaumik
content_html:
The story so far: A Supreme Court report published on Monday (August 3, 2026) makes a series of recommendations aimed at enhancing gender sensitivity in how judges write judgments and conduct proceedings in cases involving sexual offences and vulnerable persons. It replaces patriarchal language with survivor-centric terminology and recommends trauma-informed courtroom practices to prevent the re-traumatisation of victims.

Who prepared the new report?

Titled “Judgments and Gender: Sensitivity and Compassion in Writing Judgments”, the report was drafted by an expert committee headed by former Supreme Court judge and Director of the National Judicial Academy (NJA) in Bhopal, Justice Aniruddha Bose. It marks a shift from the court’s 2023 “Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes”, which focused primarily on helping judges identify and avoid gender stereotypes and patriarchal language. The new report, which will replace the earlier handbook, broadens that approach by recommending practical reforms spanning courtroom management, victim protection, judicial reasoning and trauma-informed adjudication. Before formulating its recommendations, it examined 125 trial court judgments from across the country with the assistance of State Judicial Academies.

What prompted this intervention?

The need for a new handbook arose from the Supreme Court’s February 10, 2026, judgment setting aside an Allahabad High Court ruling that had held that allegations of grabbing a 14-year-old girl’s breasts, dragging her towards a culvert and breaking the string of her lower garment amounted only to “preparation” to commit rape, rather than an “attempt” to rape. The apex court had taken cognisance of the ruling on its own after the High Court’s distinction between preparation and attempt drew widespread criticism for its apparent insensitivity.

During the proceedings, questions were also raised about the effectiveness of the Supreme Court’s 2023 handbook, issued during the tenure of former Chief Justice of India (CJI) D.Y. Chandrachud, in preventing such flawed judicial reasoning. CJI Surya Kant remarked that the handbook was “too Harvard-oriented”, suggesting that it was overly theoretical and did not adequately reflect the realities of the Indian judicial system. Justice Kant instead called for practical training, observing that it “serves no purpose to sermonise” High Court judges while sitting in the Supreme Court.

The court consequently directed the NJA in Bhopal to constitute a committee of domain experts, academics and lawyers to formulate fresh guidelines geared towards the practical training of judges.

What does it say about gender-sensitive judicial language?

The new report cautions that judicial observations rooted in stereotypes can deter survivors from reporting offences, reinforce prejudices and undermine confidence in the justice system. While both the 2023 handbook and the new report contain glossaries of terms that judges should avoid, they differ in their focus.

The 2023 handbook largely sought to replace stereotypical, colloquial or outdated expressions with neutral and legally appropriate terminology. For instance, it recommended “street sexual harassment” instead of “eve teasing”, “homemaker” instead of “housewife”, and “woman who has engaged in sexual relations outside of marriage” instead of “adulteress”. It also challenged broader assumptions about women, including stereotypes that they are inherently emotional or invariably want to have children.

The 2026 report, on the other hand, focuses more closely on problematic expressions that frequently appear in trial court judgments, particularly in sexual offence cases. Notably, it recommends replacing “prosecutrix” with “victim”, “survivor” or “complainant”, noting that the former is essentially a procedural label, while the alternatives better acknowledge the lived realities of those approaching the justice system.

The report also seeks to move judicial writing away from language that views sexual violence through the prism of morality, chastity or honour. Expressions suggesting that rape “destroyed the soul of a helpless woman”, “spoiled her childhood”, “ruined her life” or caused her to “lose her chastity” should be avoided. Instead, judges are encouraged to focus on the legal injury and its consequences — for instance, by stating that the survivor’s bodily autonomy was violated, that the offence caused severe trauma, or that its consequences require continued support and rehabilitation.

The report further urges courts to use respectful and contemporary terminology when referring to people of diverse sexual orientations and gender identities, and recommends the globally recognised framework of Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Expression and Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC).

What changes does it recommend in courtroom practices?

Beyond judicial language, the report asks judges to play an active role in ensuring that the justice process does not itself become a source of further victimisation. To this end, it sets out a series of “compassionate court practices” that judges should adopt proactively, rather than waiting for survivors to seek specific relief.

The report reiterates that trials involving rape and other sexual offences should ordinarily be held in camera (in private, closed-door proceedings) as mandated under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). It also calls for strict protection of survivors’ identities, including through the use of initials or pseudonyms in court proceedings and publications.

Describing witnesses as “guests” who assist the court in arriving at the truth, the report cautions against repeated adjournments, prolonged waiting and poor treatment that can discourage participation in the criminal justice system. Judges are also urged to enforce provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam that prohibit indecent, scandalous or needlessly offensive questions during cross-examination. In particular, the report reiterates that a survivor’s previous sexual history is immaterial in a rape trial.

A trauma-informed approach is another central recommendation. The report cautions judges against drawing adverse conclusions solely from delayed reporting, absence of physical injuries, inconsistencies in testimony or a survivor’s demeanour, noting that people respond to trauma differently. It also encourages pre-trial counselling to reduce survivors’ anxiety and help them navigate court proceedings.

title: Three from Tumakuru die in accident near Kottigehara in Chikkamagaluru
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Three people from Tumakur died, and two others suffered serious injuries when a car rammed into a truck parked near Kottigehara in Mudigere taluk of Chikkamgaluru early hours of Saturday (August 8, 2026).

The deceased have been identified as Guru Kiran (28), Mohan (30), and Jnanesh (28).

Prem Kumar and Hrithik suffered serious injuries. They have been shifted to Hassan for treatment.

They were heading to Dharmasthala in Dakshina Kannada district.

The car rammed into the truck, filled with LPG cylinders, parked near a petrol bunk. The incident occurred in Banikal police station limits.

title: J and K Police raids multiple locations in Valley to crack down on terror-related activities
author: PTI
content_html:
The Jammu and Kashmir Police counter-intelligence wing raided five districts in the valley on Saturday (August 8, 2026) to crack down on suspected terror-related activities, online misuse and alleged radicalisation networks, officials said.

Officials said the raids in Kupwara, Baramulla, Anantnag, Shopian and Bandipora were carried out in connection with FIR number 03/2023 registered at Police Station CIK, Srinagar, under Sections 505 and 153-A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), and Sections 13 and 18 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

They said electronic devices and other incriminating material were recovered and seized during the searches, which will be sent for forensic examination to further the investigation.

title: Deadline passes, posters stay put on Ernakulam Collectorate walls
author: G.  Ragesh
content_html:
Old habits die hard, and nowhere is that more evident than on the walls of the Civil Station at Kakkanad. Despite a decision to remove campaign materials affixed by various service organisations on the walls of the district administration complex by August 1, several posters continue to dot the walls and pillars of the five-storey building.

The decision to curb the rampant display of posters and flex boards on the premises of the civil station was taken at a meeting of service forums associated with various political parties on June 20. At the meeting, it was decided that a designated space would be allotted at the northern entrance of the civil station for organisations to display their announcements.

Though the promised space — five notice boards covering an entire wall — was allotted promptly, posters continue to occupy the walls in several parts of the building. Though several posters have been removed following the decision, associations affiliated with all major political parties have refused to remove all the campaign materials. Posters announcing protests and meetings of the CPI(M)-backed Kerala NGO Union and the Congress-affiliated Kerala NGO Association are among those remaining on the walls.

The NGO Union has also hung posters in different parts of the building instead of pasting them on the walls. “Our stand is that campaign materials should be displayed on all floors without defacing the walls. The decision to display them only at one designated spot is impractical as employees enter and exit the building through other entrances as well,” an NGO Union leader said. He added that whatever is left on the walls would be removed in the coming days.

A leader of the NGO Association, meanwhile, said all organisations had arrived at a consensus on the common space and that any deviation from the plan would defeat the purpose of the initiative.

title: With more passenger trains and EMUs, Sealdah station daily footfall crosses a million passengers
author: Senjuti Sengupta
content_html:
Sealdah Division of the Eastern Railway expanded its footprint across the board by introducing 68 new passenger trains, 613 additional EMU trips and 1035 additional Mail/Express (TOD) trips

The daily footfall in Sealdah Station, one of the biggest stations of the Eastern Railway has surpassed a million passengers daily in the year 2026. This comes after the Sealdah Division added 68 new passenger trains, and 613 EMUs (Electric Multiple Units) for passengers availing the railway network in the region.

"Our ultimate goal in the Sealdah Division is to ensure that every passenger feels valued from the moment they arrive at the station until they reach their destination. Whether it’s easing daily suburban commutes with AC locals, upgrading infrastructure under the Amrit Bharat scheme, or ensuring hassle-free entries with dedicated gates like the Central Gate, every step we take is focused on passenger comfort, safety, and modern convenience," said Rajeev Saxena, Divisional Railway Manager, Sealdah.  

With every new facility Sealdah Division continues to prove that public transport can be both ultra-efficient and deeply human-centric, he added.

To break bottlenecks and bring immediate relief to lakhs of daily commuters, Sealdah Division recently unveiled the Prafulla Dwar as a vital fourth gateway for the passengers accessing the station. The move has decentralised passenger movement across the terminal.

Outfitted with modern booking counters, high-visibility Train Indication Boards, and ATVMs, it turned rush-hour chaos into a smooth, organised flow. Importantly, dedicated ramps were built to ensure complete accessibility and dignified travel for passengers with disabilities.

Senior Railway officials of the division said that to take away guesswork out of daily travel and streamline passenger flow, a dedicated Platform Nomination System has been introduced at Sealdah Station.

One of the highlights of the Sealdah Division has been introduction of Air-Conditioned local trains for busy suburban routes to cater to students, tourists and those seeking healthcare at Kalyani AIIMS.

Beyond suburban travel, division expanded its footprint across the board by introducing 68 new passenger trains, 613 additional EMU trips and 1035 additional Mail/Express (TOD) trips, extending 26 existing services, and adding two new Mail/Express trains originating directly from Sealdah.

"Equipped with Automatic Ticket Vending Machines (ATVMs) for instant ticketing—giving even unreserved passengers a fast and hassle-free ticketing option—alongside a streamlined pick-up and drop-off zone right outside the gate, every detail is built for passenger comfort. With upcoming app-cab connectivity, last-mile travel will become completely effortless,” Mr. Saxena said.

The Railway officials said that under the Amrit Bharat railway station scheme Sealdah Station has undergone a striking visual and operational facelift.

Whether it’s easing daily suburban commutes with AC locals, upgrading infrastructure under the Amrit Bharat scheme, or ensuring hassle-free entries with dedicated gates like the Central Gate, every step we take is focused on passenger comfort, safety, and modern convenience," said Rajeev Saxena, Divisional Railway Manager, Sealdah.
With every new facility Sealdah Division continues to prove that public transport can be both ultra-efficient and deeply human-centric, he added.
To break bottlenecks and bring immediate relief to lakhs of daily commuters, Sealdah Division recently unveiled the Prafulla Dwar as a vital fourth gateway for the passengers accessing the station. The move has decentralised passenger movement across the terminal.
Outfitted with modern booking counters, high-visibility Train Indication Boards, and ATVMs, it turned rush-hour chaos into a smooth, organised flow. Importantly, dedicated ramps were built to ensure complete accessibility and dignified travel for passengers with disabilities.
Senior Railway officials of the division said that to take away guesswork out of daily travel and streamline passenger flow, a dedicated Platform Nomination System has been introduced at Sealdah Station.
One of the highlights of the Sealdah Division has been introduction of Air-Conditioned local trains for busy suburban routes to cater to students, tourists and those seeking healthcare at Kalyani AIIMS.
Beyond suburban travel, division expanded its footprint across the board by introducing 68 new passenger trains, 613 additional EMU trips and 1035 additional Mail/Express (TOD) trips, extending 26 existing services, and adding two new Mail/Express trains originating directly from Sealdah.
"Equipped with Automatic Ticket Vending Machines (ATVMs) for instant ticketing—giving even unreserved passengers a fast and hassle-free ticketing option—alongside a streamlined pick-up and drop-off zone right outside the gate, every detail is built for passenger comfort. With upcoming app-cab connectivity, last-mile travel will become completely effortless,” Mr. Saxena said.
The Railway officials said that under the Amrit Bharat railway station scheme Sealdah Station has undergone a striking visual and operational facelift.
